skills.title: Habitats Meet Needs
skills.description: A habitat is a place that gives plants and animals what they need to live, like food, water, shelter, and space. Can you pick how a local habitat gives these things?

skills.title: Communities in a Habitat
skills.description: A community is a group of different plants and animals that live together and affect each other in one habitat. Can you pick what helps or hurts a community's survival?

skills.title: Food Chains and Roles
skills.description: In a food chain, energy passes from producers to consumers, and decomposers break down dead things. Can you sort living things into producers, consumers, and decomposers?

skills.title: Food Webs
skills.description: A food web is many food chains linked together in a natural community. Can you pick who eats whom in a web?

skills.title: Carnivores, Herbivores, Omnivores
skills.description: Animals are grouped by what they eat: plants only, animals only, or both. Can you sort animals into herbivores, carnivores, and omnivores?

skills.title: Body Adaptations for Habitats
skills.description: Plants and animals have body parts, like webbed feet or thick bark, that help them survive in their habitats. Can you match each adaptation to its habitat?

skills.title: Limits of a Habitat
skills.description: Every habitat has only so much food, water, and space, so it can only support a certain number of living things. Can you pick why habitats have limits?

skills.title: People's Impact on Habitats
skills.description: People's activities can help or harm habitats and communities, and different people see it in different ways. Can you pick the good and bad effects?

skills.title: When a Species Disappears
skills.description: If a species becomes rare or goes extinct, its habitat and community change. Can you pick the effects and ways to stop it?

skills.title: Natural and Artificial Light
skills.description: Light comes from natural sources like the Sun and fireflies, and artificial ones like lamps and candles. Can you sort the light sources?

skills.title: Makes Light or Reflects Light
skills.description: Some things make their own light, and others only bounce light from somewhere else, like the Moon. Can you sort them?

skills.title: Properties of Light
skills.description: Light travels in straight lines. It can be absorbed, reflected, or refracted (bent). Can you match each example to what light does?

skills.title: Properties of Sound
skills.description: Sound travels as a wave through a medium like air, water, or solids. It can be absorbed, reflected, or changed. Can you pick true facts about sound?

skills.title: Vibrations Make Sound
skills.description: When something vibrates, it makes sound waves, like a guitar string or a drum. Can you pick which things make sound by vibrating?

skills.title: Materials, Light, and Sound
skills.description: Some materials let light through, block it, or bounce it, and some soak up or reflect sound. Can you match materials to what they do?

skills.title: Light With and Without Heat
skills.description: Some light sources, like bulbs and the Sun, give off lots of heat, and others, like glow sticks and LEDs, give little. Can you sort them?

skills.title: Eyes, Ears, and Devices
skills.description: Eyes and ears sense light and sound, and devices like glasses, telescopes, and microphones use light or sound. Can you match each to how it works?

skills.title: Light and Sound Devices Help Us
skills.description: Devices like cameras, sirens, and sonar affect how people live. Can you pick their good and bad effects?

skills.title: Light and Noise Pollution
skills.description: Bright lights and loud machines can bother animals, plants, and people. Can you pick the effects and ways to reduce them?

skills.title: Machines and Their Jobs
skills.description: Machines like bikes, can openers, and clocks help us do jobs in daily life. Can you match each machine to its purpose?

skills.title: Parts of Mechanisms
skills.description: Mechanisms have parts like gears, cams, cranks, belts, and levers, and each has a job. Can you label the parts and match their jobs?

skills.title: Passing Motion Along
skills.description: Gears, belts, and chains pass motion, including spinning motion, from one part to another. Can you pick how motion is passed on?

skills.title: Changing Motion
skills.description: Mechanisms can change motion from spinning to straight, or change its speed or direction. Can you match each mechanism to the change it makes?

skills.title: How Machines Change Force
skills.description: Levers, pulleys, and gears can make a force bigger or smaller, or change its direction. Can you pick how each machine changes a force?

skills.title: Machines in Daily Life Everywhere
skills.description: Machines change how people in different communities live and work. Can you pick the good and bad effects of machines?

skills.title: Comparing Machines and Nature
skills.description: Machines made for the same job, like a bike and a car, can affect the environment differently. Can you pick which harms nature less?

skills.title: The Rock Cycle
skills.description: Igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks form through cooling, packing together, and heat and pressure. Can you put the rock cycle steps in order?

skills.title: Rock Types and Their Looks
skills.description: Igneous rocks can be glassy or have crystals, sedimentary rocks have layers, and metamorphic rocks are banded. Can you match each rock to its look?

skills.title: Testing Rocks and Minerals
skills.description: We sort rocks and minerals by what they are made of and tests like hardness, colour, and streak. Can you pick the right test or group?

skills.title: Using Rocks, and Fossils
skills.description: Rocks and minerals are used for buildings, tools, and jewellery. Fossils form in sedimentary rock and tell us about Earth's past. Can you match uses and fossil facts?

skills.title: Indigenous Knowledge of Rocks
skills.description: First Nations, Métis, and Inuit peoples chose rocks and minerals for tools, art, and fire by knowing their properties. Can you match each rock to its purpose?

skills.title: Geology, Mining, and People
skills.description: Earthquakes, volcanoes, and mining affect people and nature, and recycling products helps. Can you pick the effects and ways to reduce harm?
